findings.text: H2398 (chata, to sin) carries a causative dimension not found elsewhere in the M10 corpus: one person's sin actively causes a group's sin. The repeated Kings formula says Jeroboam sinned and made Israel to sin (1 Kgs 15:30, 16:2, 16:13, 16:26, 21:22): sin is something a leader can transmit to a whole nation through example or policy, not only commit individually. The same corpus also holds the strictly individual model (Ezekiel's righteous man who sins), side by side with the leader-transmits-sin model.

findings.text: G0266 (hamartia) carries the most theologically distinctive material in the exercise: Paul's treatment of sin in Romans 5 to 8 as a near-personified ruling power, not merely an act: sin reigned in death (5:21), sold under sin (7:14), sin that dwells within me (7:17, 20), the law of sin (7:23, 8:2), slaves of sin (6:6, 17, 20). No other M10 family treats its concept as an active agent exercising dominion; every other family's moral-failure words function as acts, states or burdens, never as a ruling force with its own will. A qualitative outlier worth flagging on its own, independent of the family's broader lexical pattern.

The sin-offering system runs through this family as it did through the guilt subgroup (H0817): the same noun serves double duty for the wrong and its cultic remedy. H2401's meaning block gives sin and sin offering as one entry, and the Leviticus citations of H2403A to I are dominated by sacrificial procedure (Lev 4:3's sin offering, Exod 29:36), mirroring the guilt subgroup's H0817 pattern.
